clue.text: What dress designers might be chasing, somewhat.

definitions.text: What dress designers might be chasing
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: designers are always pursuing, going after, the latest style
second meaning: to some extent, in a rough way

explanation.walkthrough: Read word by word, the phrase describes couturiers pursuing a style; as an idiom it means only partly or roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to a limited degree, not entirely, which is what somewhat expresses.

clue.text: Peers sent to make this might be in misleading disguise.

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: its first word, meaning untrue, works as an anagram signal, and rearranging its second word gives exactly these letters

explanation.surface: Nobles dispatched on some errand might travel in deceptive costume.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer's first word works as an anagram signal acting on its second word, and that shuffle produces the clue's opening words.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretenses are disguises or shams, and false ones mislead; the legal phrase names deception used to gain something.

clue.text: March past, and you'll know it's time for Browning to like it here.

definitions.text: March past, and you'll know it's time for Browning to like it here.

parts.words: March past, and you'll know it's time for Browning to like it here
parts.note: once March is past it is April, and Robert Browning's poem Home-Thoughts, from Abroad opens 'Oh, to be in' this country 'now that April's there'

explanation.walkthrough: 'March past' looks like a military parade; it simply means once March is over. The country is the one Browning longs for in his famous poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning wrote of longing for his home country in April, so that nation is where he would like to be.

clue.text: Comes before a bet placed on such as 18-25.

indicators.note: in a down clue the bet sits on top of the next piece, so it comes first

parts.note: an ante is the stake put into the pot before a poker hand
the Ides of March is a date, so things like it are dates

explanation.surface: A wager is laid on a famous date, perhaps the day of Caesar's murder.
explanation.definitionFit: To antedate something is to precede it in time, which is coming before it.

clue.text: See 1
Leading sort of thing initially produced at 13.

definitions.text: Leading sort of thing initially produced at 13.

parts.words: Leading sort of thing initially produced at 13
parts.note: 13 is THEATER; the opening performance of a play there is the leading

explanation.walkthrough: The opening performance of a show is the first of its run and the first time it is put on before the public at a theater.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the opening evening performance of a new stage production.

clue.text: Where you might find Irish whiskey, though the grammar of the girl appeared to be crude.

definitions.text: Where you might find Irish whiskey

parts.note: a girl is referred to as she
said crudely, without the 'has', 'she has been' becomes 'she been'

explanation.surface: In an Irish pub, a girl's rough speech gives her away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'crude grammar' is dropping the auxiliary: 'she been' for 'she has been'. A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish drinking house.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an illicit Irish bar, the kind of place where whiskey, often poteen, was served.

clue.text: It may be out of place, but I'd clean it, just the same.

indicators.note: letters out of place have to be put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone will tidy up a misplaced item regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' tells you to rearrange I'D CLEAN IT; 'just the same' reads as 'all the same', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, with no difference at all between the two.

clue.text: Pro-environment crusades against man-made products? People have died this way!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, whimsically: campaigns for what is ... rather than synthetic would be ...
second meaning: death from illness or age rather than violence or accident

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally, as eco-campaigns; the second is the ordinary phrase from death certificates.
explanation.definitionFit: A death by natural causes is one from disease or old age, not from injury or foul play.

clue.text: See 8
Everything I put a label on the wrong way, otherwise it might end up as baggage, or a purse.

definitions.text: it might end up as baggage, or a purse

parts.note: everything means all

indicators.note: putting something on the wrong way round means reading the word backwards

parts.note: a tag is a label
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or else'

explanation.surface: Someone mislabels everything, so it might turn up as luggage or a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Alligator hide is a classic leather for suitcases and handbags, so the animal may end up as one.

clue.text: Turn inside out, like a female racketeer.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to turn an organ or part outward, inside out
second meaning: Chris ..., the American woman tennis champion, wielded a racket

explanation.walkthrough: 'Racketeer' suggests a gangster; here it is someone who swings a tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is a medical term for turning outward, and the surname belongs to a famous women's tennis star.

clue.text: One might manage to be set out of position on the pullback.

indicators.note: one piece is placed on, followed by, the next
letters out of position are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
read as pull back: draw means pull, written back to front

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stay in place while being pulled backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of position' gives STE; the trick is 'pullback', one word that must be split into pull (DRAW) and back, which turns it round. 'on' then attaches it, and 'to be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is someone who manages property, an estate or a household for another.

clue.text: Where 5 and 23 down might be opening.

definitions.text: Where 5 and 23 down might be opening.

parts.words: Where 5 and 23 down might be opening
parts.note: the premiere evening of a play takes place in a playhouse, where the show is opening

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is the premiere performance; a show opens at a playhouse, spelt here the American way.
explanation.definitionFit: A theater is the building where plays are staged, and so where a premiere opens.

clue.text: This way the pad is made more interesting.

definitions.note: sapid means flavorful, engaging, so it is the state of being made more interesting

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Here is how to liven up a notepad or a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals that PAD IS is made into a new word; 'This way' just points at that. Sapid is a rare word for tasty or engaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid describes something with flavor or appeal, the opposite of insipid, so it is a dressier word for interesting.

clue.text: See 2
By chance, lit in a particular science.

indicators.note: the phrase 'by chance' signals letters falling at random, and the fodder starts with the word chance itself

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A discovery made by luck, lighting up some branch of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By chance' looks like an adverb phrase; its second word doubles as part of the letters to shuffle, CHANCE plus LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical language belongs to a specialized field, such as one branch of science or a trade.

clue.text: Hit on the golf course, as wrist-movement might reveal.

indicators.note: the first piece sits on top of the second in a down clue

parts.note: to cuff is to strike with the open hand
links is a golf course, especially a seaside one

explanation.surface: A golfer strikes the ball, and the flick of the wrist tells the story.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' sets the hit above the golf course. Cufflinks fasten shirt cuffs and peep out when the wrist moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cufflinks are fasteners for shirt cuffs, glimpsed at the wrist when the arm moves.

clue.text: Someone evidently thought it a good time to take a stab at solving the country's problems.

definitions.text: Someone evidently thought it a good time to take a stab at solving the country's problems.

parts.words: Someone evidently thought it a good time to take a stab at solving the country's problems
parts.note: Brutus and his fellow conspirators stabbed Julius Caesar on the 15th day of the third Roman month in 44 BC, claiming to save Rome

explanation.walkthrough: 'take a stab at' means to try, but here the stabbing is literal: Caesar's assassination on the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides was the Roman name for the 15th of March, the day Caesar was stabbed to death.

clue.text: A temporary change of direction preceded what the 24 did in defense, perhaps.

definitions.text: what the 24 did in defense, perhaps

parts.note: a tack is a sailing boat's change of course against the wind
to lead is to go before, so led means preceded

explanation.surface: A brief swerve came before what the defender did.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is LINEMAN, an American football player, who tackles ball carriers when defending.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football, defensive linemen tackle the opposing ball carrier to bring him down.

clue.text: One doesn't like to do it, putting it mildly.

definitions.text: One doesn't like to do it, putting it mildly.

parts.words: One doesn't like to do it, putting it mildly
parts.note: saying someone 'doesn't like' a thing is an understatement of condemning it strongly

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as reluctance to do something; it means that 'doesn't like' is a mild way of saying the stronger verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore is to disapprove strongly, so merely not liking something understates it.

clue.text: What we might be told is an old list of possible jurors.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stories, things recounted to us

definitions.text: an old list of possible jurors
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in old law, a list of bystanders summoned to make up a short jury

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense survives in 'talesman', a juror summoned from bystanders.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stories, and historically the writ or roll summoning spare jurors to fill a panel.

clue.text: No agent, however disguised, shows such capacity.

indicators.note: a word disguised has its letters scrambled into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: No secret operative, however well disguised, can do such a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage measures how much cargo a ship can carry, its carrying capacity.

clue.text: Look, there's absolutely nothing in it to be old and feeble!

indicators.note: something placed in it goes inside the other word

parts.note: look means see
nil means nothing at all

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker dismisses something empty as worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Senile describes weakness of body or mind brought on by great age.

clue.text: To depreciate a headache, a penicillin extraction is obviously the answer.

indicators.note: the answer is extracted, drawn out of the run of letters

parts.note: the answer runs across these words

explanation.surface: For a headache, a dose of penicillin is the obvious cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraction' sounds medical, like drawing a drug from mold; it signals letters taken from inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheapen something is to lower its value or worth, which is depreciating it.

clue.text: See 5
Possibly the center or end of one climbing a pole, perhaps.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in American football the center and the ends play on the line, as linemen
second meaning: a worker who climbs poles to repair telephone or power lines

explanation.walkthrough: 'center or end' looks like positions in a word; they are positions on an American football line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a football player on the line of scrimmage and a utility worker who services overhead wires.

clue.text: See 18 across
Hot to catch a girl with nothing on?

definitions.text: Hot to catch a girl with nothing on?

indicators.note: nothing is added on after the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An eager suitor wants to snare an undressed girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, a cowboy keen to rope someone, and the wordplay: a girl with nothing tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is the rope a cowboy throws to catch an animal, the tool for someone keen to catch.

clue.text: It might not be much good without stock attached to it, but it's often rifled.

definitions.text: It might not be much good without stock attached to it
definitions.meaning: first description: a firearm's tube is little use without the stock, the wooden shoulder piece fixed to it
second description: the inside of the tube is usually rifled, cut with spiral grooves to spin the bullet

explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' and 'rifled' suggest a shop that has been robbed; both are terms for parts of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The barrel is the tube of a firearm, fixed to the stock and grooved inside to spin the bullet.

clue.text: Hardly an agreeable way to behave.

definitions.text: Hardly an agreeable way to behave.

parts.words: Hardly an agreeable way to behave
parts.note: agreeable here means given to agreeing; refusing to agree is the opposite of that

explanation.walkthrough: 'agreeable' seems to mean pleasant, but it means inclined to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement with an accepted view, the reverse of going along with it.

clue.text: What one is supposed to view isn't stated, but agitation is obvious when something does.

definitions.text: agitation is obvious when something does

parts.words: What one is supposed to view
parts.note: see means view, here as an instruction to look at something
the thing to be looked at is left off, so only the little article in front of it remains

explanation.surface: An unseen spectacle, but the stirring it causes is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first half as an order to look at 'the …' whose object is never said: SEE THE, with the noun missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to churn or boil, so a seething thing shows obvious agitation.
